# Lab 5.4: User-Defined Aggregate Functions

## What We Are Going to Do
Create a SQL aggregate function and a JavaScript aggregate function, and use them in GROUP BY queries.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Two SQL UDAFs, one with a non-aggregate argument.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE OR REPLACE AGGREGATE FUNCTION lab05.weighted_avg(x FLOAT64, w FLOAT64)
RETURNS FLOAT64
AS (SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(x * w), SUM(w)));

CREATE OR REPLACE AGGREGATE FUNCTION lab05.pct_above(x FLOAT64, threshold FLOAT64 NOT AGGREGATE)
RETURNS FLOAT64
AS (ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(COUNTIF(x &gt; threshold), COUNT(x)) * 100, 1));

SELECT p.category,
       ROUND(lab05.weighted_avg(i.sale_price, 1), 2) AS avg_sale,
       lab05.pct_above(i.sale_price, 100) AS pct_over_100
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` i
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.products` p ON p.id = i.product_id
GROUP BY p.category
ORDER BY pct_over_100 DESC;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   `threshold` is marked `NOT AGGREGATE`, so it is one fixed value for the whole group, not a column.

2. **[SQL] A JavaScript UDAF.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE TEMP AGGREGATE FUNCTION js_geo_mean(x FLOAT64)
RETURNS FLOAT64
LANGUAGE js AS r'''
  export function initialState() { return {logSum: 0, n: 0}; }
  export function aggregate(state, x) { if (x &gt; 0) { state.logSum += Math.log(x); state.n++; } }
  export function merge(state, partial) { state.logSum += partial.logSum; state.n += partial.n; }
  export function finalize(state) { return state.n ? Math.exp(state.logSum / state.n) : null; }
''';

SELECT department, ROUND(js_geo_mean(retail_price), 2) AS geo_mean_price
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.products`
GROUP BY department;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| SQL UDAF | Many rows → one value per group |
| `NOT AGGREGATE` | Argument fixed for the whole group |
| JS UDAF | `initialState`, `aggregate`, `merge`, `finalize` |
| Routine type | `AGGREGATE_FUNCTION` |
